subject: P95/P99 latency: traffic shaping, streaming fallback & test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & immediate asks — p95/p99 acceptance criteria

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery focused on end-to-end (client → your edge → Redwood hosted API → model → back to user) latency qualification:

- Target thresholds you mentioned: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 410ms for single-turn text generation (median workload). You also noted heavier tails during peak batch ingestion windows.
- Streaming (chunked token delivery) is required for chat UX; you expect 20–30 tokens/sec per session on average during normal traffic, spikes up to ~80 tokens/sec.
- Concurrency: baseline 800 active sessions, peak bursts to ~2,800 simultaneous open connections during campaign-driven events.
- Throughput: 12k requests/day currently, with 65% sitting in short sessions (<= 8 tokens).

Immediate asks so we can scope a hosted qualification run:
1) Please share a traffic profile CSV (timestamped RPS, typical token counts per request, proportion streaming vs non-streaming). A stub example attached.
2) Confirm SLO window: do you accept a 30-day rolling measurement for p95/p99, or do you prefer a shorter pre-cut (we normally run a 7‑day evaluation window for initial acceptance).
3) Any IP allowlist / egress constraints we should know about for the test harness?

Ben and Mateo — copying you in; Ben can help define the streaming concurrency ramp and Mateo will draft the probe schedule & runbook after we get the traffic CSV.

Next steps: Sarah to return traffic CSV + any procurement constraints by Wed 3/3 EOD. We’ll propose two 3-hour windows for a controlled canary run (one baseline, one peak-replay) and a fall-back plan to route to an incumbent model variant if we see tail violations.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: example_traffic_profile_stub.csv (3 rows sample)
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@veridian.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & immediate asks — p95/p99 acceptance criteria

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear summary. Attaching the traffic CSV you requested (veridian_traffic_profile_v1.csv). A few notes:
- The CSV has 1-minute granularity for the last 30 days; tokens/request is an approximate field (we sample 1 in 100 requests).
- Streaming proportion is ~48% of calls by count, but accounts for ~72% of token volume.
- Peak replay window on Feb 14 shows ~2,700 concurrent sessions for a 25-minute spike.

SLO window: Procurement prefers a 30-day rolling measurement but we can agree to a staged acceptance: 7-day technical qualification (non-binding) followed by a 30-day production evaluation tied to go/no-go.

IP/egress: No special outbound restrictions. We will provide a short list of IPs for allowlist during the test.

I'll loop in procurement separately for contract terms.

Best,
Sarah
Senior Product Manager — Veridian.ai
sarah.kim@veridian.ai

Attachment: veridian_traffic_profile_v1.csv (attached)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@veridian.ai>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & immediate asks — p95/p99 acceptance criteria

Thanks Sarah — the CSV is helpful. A couple of immediate clarifications / technical asks from our side:

1) Tokenization: Which tokenizer do you use server-side? Byte-level BPE, or a variant? We want to make sure our probe generator matches tokens/request distribution.
2) Client-side timeouts: What are the client socket timeouts for streaming sessions? Short client timeouts can create noisy tail measurements.
3) Are there any hotspots (per-region) in the traffic? The CSV has geo, but if you can call out the top 3 regions, that helps with routing decisions for the canary.

Proposed test windows (subject to your IP allowlist):
- Baseline run: Thu 3/11 02:00–05:00 UTC (low background noise)
- Peak replay: Thu 3/11 18:00–21:00 UTC (we will replay the 25-minute peak across a 3-hour window to reproduce tail events and observe graceful degradation)

For streaming SLOs we usually measure token-first-byte latency at p95/p99 and an overall end-to-end p95/p99 on complete-response time. Fallback plan: if token-first-byte p99 > 700ms for >1% of sampling during peak replay, we perform an automated model-fallback to a lower-latency variant and mark the run as requiring remediation.

I can script the probe generation once we have tokenizer info and the final allowlist.

- Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@veridian.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & immediate asks — p95/p99 acceptance criteria

All —

Draft runbook attached (redwood_slo_probe_plan.pdf). Highlights:
- Measurement windows: we’ll run two 3-hour controlled windows as Ben suggested. Each window will include: warm-up (20 mins), steady-state replay (2 hours), and tail exercise (40 mins) where we force interleaved short/long sessions to stress KV cache & batching.
- Metrics collected: token-first-byte, end-to-end request-completion, model-inference-only, edge-ingress latency, and per-connection failure rate.
- Data retention: we’ll provide raw trace samples for the 7-day technical qualification and aggregate SLO reporting for the 30-day evaluation.
- Canary rollback: automated fallback to quantized gpt-variant on token-first-byte p99 breach > 600ms sustained for 1000 samples.

Questions for Veridian:
A) Can you confirm whether the client aggregates tokens and re-sends partial frames during network blips (this affects how we interpret streaming gaps)?
B) For the peak replay, do you want exact temporal fidelity (replay timestamps preserved) or amplitude-scaled (we compress the 25-minute spike across the 3-hour window to simulate a longer tail)?

I’ve scheduled the probe infra: we’ll start provisioning GPU instances on Mon 3/8 once the allowlist and tokenizer are confirmed.

-Mateo
Staff SRE, Performance — Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_slo_probe_plan.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@veridian.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & immediate asks — p95/p99 acceptance criteria

Thanks everyone — practical next steps so we’re aligned:

1) Sarah / Veridian: please send tokenizer details + final IP allowlist by EOD today (3/3). If procurement needs a draft statement of work, let me know and I’ll push a short SOW template.
2) Ben: prepare the probe generator with conservative tokenization assumptions (we’ll re-run once tokenizer confirmed).
3) Mateo: hold provisioning until allowlist/tokenizer arrive; once confirmed, start infra on Mon 3/8 and I’ll book the two 3-hour windows on Thu 3/11 per Ben’s proposal.
4) All: I’ll prepare a one-page acceptance rubric that maps observed metrics (token-first-byte p95/p99 and end-to-end p95/p99) to pass/warn/fail bins for the 7-day technical qualification vs 30-day production evaluation.

If anyone needs to push dates, flag now — otherwise I’ll follow up with the calendar invites and SOW draft.

Cheers,
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Bcc: procurement@veridian.ai (separate procurement thread for contract terms)
